EQP_Jaheira
Jaheira is a recruitable companion. She and  Minsc return from both Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn and are the only two recruitable companions who cannot be romanced.[1] She is a high half-elf and a druid[2] with the Soldier background, and can be first found at the Last Light Inn during Act Two.

Having become High Harper in the century since her first adventures, wherein her husband Khalid was killed, Jaheira is deadset on maintaining her Harper network, taking down the Cult of the Absolute, and later reuniting with Minsc, her closest friend. Jaheira is known for her sharp wit and dry humour, and also serves as a mentor figure to the rest of the party.

“
Nature's servant awaits.
„
— Jaheira's catchphrase

Overview

Starting class

When first encountered, Jaheira is a level 8 druid with the following ability scores: 15 STR, 14 DEX, 17 CON, 10 INT, 16 WIS, 15 CHA. If recruited, she reverts to a level 1 druid with the standard ability scores for the class. Her default subclass is the Circle of the Land. Jaheira has the Soldier background.

Personal quest

If recruited, Jaheira has a companion quest called The High Harper.

Recruitment

Jaheira can be fully recruited near the end of Act Two, after  Ketheric Thorm retreats to the Mind Flayer Colony. Until then, she is only available as an attached follower. However, if the Last Light Inn is destroyed and the party is still allied with Jaheira after Ketheric is defeated, she can be offered a place at camp. Although she accepts, she is, in this case, not available as a companion until Act Three.

If Jaheira dies before she is recruited as a full companion, she remains  Dead and cannot be recruited. If she is killed by the  Dark Urge's hand, they earn the inspiration ⁠Forced Retirement.

Leaving the party

If the player character kills  Minsc during her quest line, refuses to recruit him if he is freed, sacrifices him for  Sarevok, kills any of her children, kills  Isobel, intimidates her into leaving after obtaining the Slayer form, or – as the Dark Urge – embraces taking up the mantle of Bhaal's Chosen following their fight with  Orin, then Jaheira permanently leaves the party.

Approval

Main article: Jaheira/Approval

Jaheira favours direct approaches and eschews flattery. She loves snarky jokes, even at her own expense.[3]

Romance

Unlike in Baldur's Gate II, Jaheira cannot be romanced in Baldur's Gate 3.

Description

Appearance

Tall and lean, Jaheira wears her silvery-chestnut hair in neatly braided rows wrapped in blue cloth, with silver ringlets at their temples. Her green-gold eyes, high cheekbones and tapered ears lend her hawk-like profile an air of alert poise, revealing her elven ancestry. Approximately 150 years old when the game's events start to unfold, faint war lines etch the skin at the corners of her mouth and brow, softening only when a rare smile surfaces.

Battle and age have sharpened her insight and weathered her frame, but not dulled her agility or the blades of the two curved scimitars she carries on her back, marking her as both warrior and druid.

Personality

Jaded and strengthened by her past, Jaheira is a formidable, headstrong and opinionated woman. Charismatic and insightful, she has a sharp tongue, and her wit can be deprecating to those for whom it is meant. She tends to make jokes out of serious situations and approves of the player character doing so.[4] Despite being a wizened veteran of numerous wars, she maintains a healthy sense of humour and does not mind when she is the butt of a good joke.[5]

As a result of Jaheira's experiences during her long life, she is rarely surprised and; except for what concerns those close to her heart, like Minsc; takes unexpected events calmly and in stride. Her initial testing of the player character with truth-telling drugs, as well as her inquisitive reaction to the Dark Urge revealing their nature as a Bhaalspawn, shows that she is very cautious with whom she extends her trust. But once the party prove themselves, Jaheira is a loyal and stalwart ally who sees them as equals, never afraid to speak her mind and not sugarcoating the truth.

However, although Jaheira outwardly displays assuredness, confidence, and steadfast certainty of Harper virtues, such as hope and bravery prevailing in the face of evil, she may, like many leaders, reveal doubts about these things if approached in moments of self-reflection or great significance to her.[6]

As one of the eldest and strongest of Baldur's Gate's Harpers, she commands the respect of most of the organisation. Speaking to Harpers with Jaheira in the party reveals that they almost always defer to her strength and experience. Her military background shows in her professionalism and cold analysis when dealing with most situations. One of the few exceptions to this is her old friend  Minsc, whom Jaheira initially believed to be dead due to a combination of Minsc's recklessness and her own desire to put the safety of all Baldur's Gate above individual lives. She becomes enraged when it is revealed he was alive and being manipulated by Orin's Doppelgängers using her face. Once they reunite, their relationship is initially strained due to Jaheira not believing Minsc could be so easily manipulated, though they do eventually reaffirm their friendship.

Backstory

See  Jaheira for full backstory[7]

Jaheira was born in the nation of  Tethyr to one of the nobles loyal to the king. When she was only a year old, a Tethyrian civil war broke out, and her family was killed by a mob of angry peasants. One of the servant girls took Jaheira, fled into the forest of Tethyr, and stumbled upon an enclave of druids. They took her in and raised her as their own. Jaheira grew up very headstrong and militant in her beliefs that the only way to protect nature is to have an active role in the world.

At some point, Jaheira was introduced to the Harpers and joined them. There she met and fell in love with another half-elf named Khalid, whom she saved from an attempted assassination by the  Shadow Thieves. And though they had completely different characters, they married soon after and travelled the  Sword Coast together.

The Iron Crisis & Shadows of Amn

During the events of the first Baldur's Gate game, Jaheira and Khalid were sent by the Harpers to investigate the  Iron Crisis and the  Nashkel mines. In the  Friendly Arm Inn, they waited for their old friend  Gorion but met his ward instead. They travelled with Gorion's Ward (the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games) to investigate the crisis which led to their confrontation with the culprit –  Sarevok Anchev.

Sometime after Sarevok's defeat, the group parted ways for a while until they once again joined up alongside their friends, Gorion's Ward,  Imoen,  Minsc, and  Dynaheir. After they left Baldur's Gate, they were captured by Shadow Thieves and imprisoned in a dungeon beneath the city of  Athkatla in  Amn. She, Minsc and Imoen survived, but Dynaheir and Jaheira's beloved husband Khalid were killed. Their captor was  Jon Irenicus – an elven wizard who wanted to steal the Bhaalspawn essence for himself. She eventually helped Gorion's Ward defeat him.

Crusade against Ketheric

About 20 years later, Jaheira, alongside Harpers and druids of the  Emerald Enclave, fought  Ketheric Thorm and his forces of  Shar at Moonrise Towers. Their unified forces managed to defeat Thorm and imprison him within his family's Mausoleum in Reithwin Town. The united army was scattered when Ketheric brought down the Shadow Curse upon the surrounding lands, twisting them into a horrifying place of deadly shadows and cursed beings.

Life in Baldur's Gate

At some point later, Jaheira made herself a home in Baldur's Gate, where she raised her foster children:  Jord,  Rion,  Jhessem,  Fig and  Tate. Yet, a Harper's life demanded she spend much time away from her home and children.

She has a private basement that looks like a Druid's cavern, and it is heavily trapped. The basement is inhabited by the Postmaster Badger and his messenger rats, whom he trains to be harper spies.

Jaheira keeps a key under a trapped bookcase. It unlocks a secret door hidden behind the bookcase, where she keeps some of her most private items:  Rite of the Timeless Body,  Belm,  Staff of the Ram, and  Khalid's Gift.[8]

After Minsc was rescued from his stone prison, they reunited once again. They were the first to uncover information about the threat of the Absolute. Due to Minsc's impulsivity and eagerness to fight, he was captured by the cultists. Jaheira, realising they were severely unprepared against the cult, decided to leave him in order to warn others with news about the cult. She later regretted how easily she made the decision to leave him behind, knowing he would never have done the same to her.

Last Light Inn

After learning of Ketheric's return, Jaheira quartered herself with a squad of Harpers at Last Light Inn, in the middle of the Shadow-Cursed Lands. From there, her scouts ventured forth to keep a close watch on the cult's forces at Moonrise Towers.

Since she left her family for Last Light Inn, they received only one  sending message from her. It read: "I'm sorry, you know what to do."

Involvement

“
Unshackled from shadows, she will rise in moonlit glory and carve a path of brightness to the accursed one's second death. So sayeth the wise  Alaundo.
„
— Jaheira on Dame Aylin

Act One

Although she is not present during Act One, the party can stumble across a hint to her. In Grymforge, they can find a dead drow named  Jhaam in one of the cages near  Murmath at X: -632 Y: 388. It is possible to use  Speak with Dead on her, revealing she was sent by Jaheira to investigate rumours of Absolutist activity in Grymforge, as well as their attempts to find potential weapons. If Jaheira has not been met yet, the companions comment on whether or not they recognise her name. Only  Karlach knows exactly who she is, while  Astarion and  Wyll have heard of her and  Lae'zel,  Shadowheart, and  Gale have no clue.[9]

Act Two

On reaching the Last Light Inn, Jaheira is instantly wary of the party and summons vines to stop the player character.[10] She produces a  Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen.[11] Suspicious that the ensnared player character may be a True Soul, she demonstrates how the tadpoles react to those infected by bringing the specimen up to their face. It moves excitedly in its bottle, reinforcing her belief that the party is comprised of True Souls. Either  Mol (if the tieflings were saved) or  Marcus (if not saved) comes to their aid, vouching for them.

Jaheira is shocked at how anyone clearly infected somehow manages to have free will and demands answers. She insists on knowing the whole truth. If given vague answers, a  DC 21 Persuasion Check is required to convince her to back down, while showing her the  Mysterious Artefact convinces her to relent without a check. She then invites the party inside the inn for a drink, granting the ⁠Living Legend inspiration to party members with the  Entertainer background.

If the wine is smelled first, a hint of Klauthgrass is detected – a truth serum:

  • [MEDICINE] Smell the wine first. (DC 10)
  • [DRUID] [MEDICINE] Smell the wine. (DC 6 )
  • [ROGUE] [INSIGHT] Meet her stare head on as you examine her body language. (DC 6 )
    • [MEDICINE] Sniff the wine to see if it's been tampered with. (DC 6 )

The party can still down the wine, even knowing there is a truth serum:

  • [CONSTITUTION] Despite knowing you're under the effects of a drug, try to deny the tadpole has any influence over you. (DC 6)

Depending on the option chosen, the following inspiration can be gained

  • ⁠From One Hero to Another ( Folk Hero background) – for downing the drink
  • ⁠Not My First Time ( Charlatan background) – successfully passing the constitution check to resist the wine
  • ⁠Wary of Strangers ( Urchin background) – for refusing the drink

Jaheira's trust can be earned regardless of whether her altered drink is consumed, and her query is the same: Is the parasite changing the party? Jaheira refuses to believe an assertion that the parasite isn't doing anything, but does believe a statement that the player character is resisting the urge to change.

Once Jaheira trusts the party, she explains the situation: that the leader of Moonrise Towers is  Ketheric Thorm, who is immensely powerful and gifted with immortality. The Harpers are attempting to find a way to stop the cult and kill Thorm once and for all. They have had little luck, but Jaheira believes the party can make a difference by infiltrating Moonrise as a True Soul. She asks the party to go upstairs and meet  Isobel, the one responsible for shielding the Last Light Inn.

Isobel's abduction

After Jaheira starts to trust the party, she refers them upstairs to gain a blessing from Isobel. When Marcus arrives to abduct her, the party can help him or try to stop him, which starts ⁠Resolve the Abduction. If Isobel is captured or killed, everyone in the tavern except for Jaheira and the party is killed and turned into a shadow-cursed zombie. The party can lie to Jaheira, telling her they tried to stop Marcus. Jaheira can be invited to stay at their camp, but she does not become a companion until ⁠Infiltrate Moonrise Towers is complete.

Assault on Moonrise Towers

If Isobel is saved, Jaheira continues to operate from Last Light Inn until the party is ready to defeat Thorm once and for all. When ⁠Find Ketheric Thorm's Relic is complete, Jaheira and her Harpers have already started the assault on the Moonrise Towers.[12] If  Dame Aylin is spared, Jaheira sees her assaulting Moonrise Towers.

Jaheira can be invited to join the party as an attached follower until getting to the tower top and defeating Ketheric for the first time. If not invited, she fights alongside the party in the assault. Jaheira is neither shy about wading into melee combat nor discriminating about who she engages (e.g., against enemies who deal significant damage). As such, it is quite easy for her to die, and, because she is not a companion at this point, she cannot be revived if killed here. If the party intend to have her as a companion later, it is advisable to keep her well protected, or not invite her (as an attached companion) to participate in the battle.

When Ketheric escapes to the Mind Flayer Colony, Jaheira can be recruited as a full companion. If not recruited, but acting as an attached follower, she stays at the tower top until his defeat. After Ketheric Thorm is defeated there, she can be found on the main floor, where she may ask to join the party on her own.

Act Three

Meeting the Harpers

If Jaheira is recruited and in the party when they reach Wyrm's Crossing, she asks to visit the Harper safehouse in a shop called Danthelon's Dancing Axe. This starts her companion quest, ⁠The High Harper, to rescue her old friend  Minsc.

Upon entering the shop and speaking to the shopkeeper,  Entharl Danthelon greets the party, although Jaheira tells him to skip the pleasantries if she is present. Entharl gives the key to a secret room at X: -18 Y: 138, where the Harpers are waiting down the iron ladder.

Once down below, Harper  Geraldus greets the party with a strange greeting – "May Selûne's Tears shine on this meeting." He again emphasises Selûne's Tears a few moments later. A successful Insight check reveals that Geraldus is not nervous, but terrified, and is using Selûne's Tears as a code. Jaheira mentions that the Harpers remind her of  Marcus, implying they are traitors laying a trap. Choosing to strike while Jaheira has them distracted makes the enemies  Surprised.

After the Harpers are defeated, they revert to their natural form as doppelgangers. Geraldus explains that the rest of the Harpers were murdered or dragged away, while he was only kept alive to lay a trap for Jaheira. Disillusioned at this revelation, Jaheira suggests the life of a Harper might be unsuited for Geraldus, as he endangered Entharl and others by going along with the doppelganger's plans, but she can be persuaded to think otherwise. Either way, Geraldus leaves, and Jaheira explains the main reason she sought out the Harpers was for more information on  Minsc of Rashemen, who she had sent them after. Previously, Minsc and Jaheira had been investigating the cult together, but were separated, and Jaheira had to leave him behind so she could spread word of the cult to others.

With the Harpers gone, Jaheira needs a moment to think. She tells the party she has some ideas on how to proceed, but wants to consider whether this is truly her last resort. After arriving in the Lower City, she explains her plan to enlist the help of the Guild and  Nine-Fingers Keene.

In the Guildhall

Keene is in her office, well aware of the Harpers' entrance into her territory. She informs the party that she already knows of Minsc, who is going by the new title of the Stone Lord, that he now works for the Absolute, and is decimating the members of the Guild. As he threatens the Guild, she intends to take him down, but refuses to let the party confront Minsc themselves. However, there are plenty of other members with loose lips who eventually reveal the Guild's intention to ambush Minsc at the vaults of the Counting House.

The vaults of the Counting House

“
That old elf took two guards by herself. And she wasn't even scratched.
„
— Cashguard Morra, commenting on Jaheira's combat prowess after the battle in the vaults

Once inside the vaults, the deepest area of the room is straight ahead. The party must move forward beyond the locked door. Minsc can then finally be seen in the flesh. Unfortunately, Minsc disappears before he can be confronted, and a group of Bhaalists attack the party as a parting gift.

Once the Bhaalists have been defeated, the party must search for clues on where Minsc went. Approaching the large vault at the end of the room X: -691 Y: 873 (which was completely smashed by Minsc) with a successful perception check shows mud from the sewers.

The Sewers

Minsc can be found in the Abandoned Cistern. There are two ways to find Minsc: belowground and aboveground.

  • Belowground, it is necessary to jump the pipes above the caustic water at X: -186 Y: 883 and defeat the Bhaalists guarding the area. Going north, there is an area with a Sluice Valve, which is stuck. A successful athletic check opens it. Otherwise, it is necessary to interact with the temperature valve and the water level valve, timing them properly to open the door. The sluice tunnel leads to Minsc.
  • Aboveground, there is a garden area north of the Steel Watch Foundry with a door that says, "Keep Out." There are two pressure plates on the north and south walls of the room. Moving a party member (or one of the crates in the room) on each of them at the same time opens the door to a secret area. In this area is an ornate hatch which leads to the area where Minsc is.

Facing Minsc

After finding Minsc again, he is under the control of a tadpole and does not see reason. He immediately attacks the party, along with a number of doppelgangers, cultists, and a Zhentarim. All Absolutists must be defeated. Taking down the "Jaheira" doppelganger elicits some panicked voice lines from Minsc. If the Zhentarim survive, they are found later in the Guildhall.

If Minsc dies here, Jaheira becomes enraged, slanders the party, and leaves permanently, concluding the quest. To avoid this, Minsc must be knocked out with a non-lethal attack.

The Emperor initially refuses to bring Minsc under his protection, stating he is too far gone to help. However, he can be convinced to bring Minsc under protection, particularly with Jaheira present. If Jaheira is not present, Minsc can still be shown images of Jaheira alive and well, allowing him to be recruited. If Jaheira is dead, Minsc cannot be recruited.

If the player character agrees with the Emperor on not saving Minsc after he is knocked out, or decides to kill him themselves, the outcome is the same as if Minsc is killed in combat: Jaheira leaves the party. If she is not present in the Abandoned Cistern, she automatically starts a dialogue upon the party's return to camp, and permanently leaves afterwards.

If Minsc is successfully recruited, he rushes off to find his friend  Boo, smashing through several walls to the north. Following him and subsequently talking to Minsc and Jaheira resolves the quest ⁠The High Harper.

At some point after recruiting Minsc, Jaheira and Minsc have an argument where the latter refers to her as his wychlaran, and the player character must intervene. They have the option here to try convincing Minsc to rely more on Jaheira, and this choice determines which of two possible outcomes Jaheira's story has, leading to slight differences in her dialogue and behaviour at the dinner party in the Epilogue.

Ending

Jaheira's ending depends on whether or not she decides to retire from the Harpers after a very long lifetime of fighting for Baldur's Gate. In order for her to retire, the player character must find the  Rite of the Timeless Body in the secret basement of Elerrathin's Home with her in the party, and then speak with her about it.

Depending on whether the player character has at least 60 approval with her, Jaheira may either keep the scroll or burn it. If she decides to keep the scroll, the player character may try to speak with her about it again at a later point after her approval has increased.

Retirement from the Harpers

If the player character has sufficient approval, she decides to burn the scroll, feeling that Baldur's Gate is in safe hands. She retires from the Harpers and settles down as a stay-at-home mother. When spoken with at the reunion celebration, Jaheira shares that she has done much more sitting down than she would like, but has been heavily involved in the lives of her children, who have proven themselves capable of restoring the city on their own. She confesses that she misses adventuring and that Baldur's Gate is, in fact, her home, but she remarks on how one only realises someplace is home once they leave it and look back.

Remaining the High Harper

If the player character did not convince Jaheira to retire, she keeps the scroll, which allows her to extend her life further, as she feels she is not done protecting Baldur's Gate yet from the Dead Three. When spoken with at the reunion celebration, Jaheira states that she has to house people and rebuild the Harper network; she has little love for Baldur's Gate, but she chose to keep serving the city for her family.

Other dialogue at the reunion party

If the player character speaks with Jaheira during the reunion celebration, regardless of ending, Jaheira talks of Baldur's Gate's reconstruction efforts and the roles her children, the Harpers and Minsc, have to play in it. She reveals that Jord has joined the Harpers and is planning crop cycles in Wyrm's Crossing. Rion has temporarily joined the Flaming Fist, but she mostly spends her time incarcerating corrupt Fists. If the player character asks her if they may join the Harpers, she always agrees, even if they are a mind flayer; otherwise, she asks the player character what "home" means to them. She then either teases or comforts the player character based on their response before dismissing herself to ensure no one tampers with the drinks.

Speak with Dead

Jaheira has  Speak with Dead dialogue that unfolds depending on events that have passed:

  • Who are you?
    • Jaheira
      Harper... Jaheira...
  • What happened to you?
    • Jaheira
      Stood... against... Bhaal... (if witnessed the player accept Bhaal)
    • Jaheira
      Stood... against... Absolute...
  • Did you find Minsc?
    • Jaheira
      Too... far... gone...
  • What were you doing?
    • Jaheira
      Hunting... Absolute... hunted... in turn... (if in Act Two)
    • Jaheira
      What... needed... to be done... (if witnessed the player accept Bhaal)
    • Jaheira
      Helping... a friend...
  • What should I tell your family?
    • Narrator
      *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.*
  • I saw you with Minsc in the Counting House - what happened?
    • Jaheira
      Shape... shifter... sworn to... Orin...
  • Any regrets in life?
    • Jaheira
      ...HAH!...
  • How do I save the city?
    • Narrator
      *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.*

Trivia

  • In Baldur's Gate 3, Jaheira is voiced by Tracy Wiles, replacing Heidi Shannon from previous games.
  • Her face in Baldur's Gate 3 matches her portrait from Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn.

Bugs

  • Jaheira is supposed to turn hostile whenever  Isobel is attacked by a playable character in Moonrise Towers. However, because the game does not check the source of the attack, Jaheira turns hostile whenever Isobel is harmed or takes damage from any source after defeating Ketheric on the Moonrise Towers Rooftop (e.g., walking over  Caustic Brine set by Absolute Zealots when entering Moonrise Towers after Ketheric is killed).
  • If Jaheria is recruited, a bug may manifest which causes her to, in many respects, not be considered a party member (or even an ally), though she remains fully controllable as one. It can trigger as early as her being recruited after the party return to Moonrise Towers from the final defeat of Ketheric Thorm. The bug appears to make Jaheira almost always remain a neutral non-combatant, even when she clearly should not remain so, and all other party members are scripted or flagged to enter combat. Once activated, this "neutral flag" remains until she makes an attack, which commits her to turn-based combat mode. The following are some detailed examples of the effects of this bug:
    • Spells targeting allies cannot be cast on her (in case of target selection) or do not include her (in case of AoE party buffs) unless she is the one casting the spell.
    • Enemies usually do not consider her a member of the party and thus ignore her, and allow her to remain out of combat, unless she herself attacks. She remains free to roam these areas, interact with objects there, and cast non-combat spells while otherwise avoiding combat.
      • If the other party members enter turn-based combat automatically due to starting a conflict, she remains out of combat unless she was the one starting the conflict.
      • If the party enter an area where conflict automatically starts against them (e.g., the Ancient Lair or the Counting House High Security Vaults), she remains out of combat unless she attacks.
        • If a scripted event that begins combat specifically designates Jaheira as a target, as with  Sarevok Anchev at the Murder Tribunal, then she enters combat as normal.
      • If Jaheira is not in combat, she can make a single attack against creatures under the effect of  Sanctuary.
      • If the other party members are in combat while Jaheira is not, and she then stealthily attacks, passes the required checks to remain hidden, and lands a killing blow on her first attack, she remains out of combat. This makes her an ideal candidate to respec as a high-level rogue and use sneak attacks to finish off sufficiently weakened opponents, while the rest of the party remains in turn-based combat.
      • The Ancient Lair exhibits further unusual behaviour: If Jaheira is alone there (an area where combat begins automatically) and she attacks in stealth mode while passing the required Stealth checks to remain hidden, she can then immediately leave stealth without consequence; the opponents there will continue to ignore her and search for the assailant, even if she is right next to them. This behaviour usually does not manifest elsewhere. However, if Jaheira attacks at a close enough range where the target (if they survive) or others notice the attack, combat then begins for her as normal.
    • If Jaheira kills an opponent out of combat (even while the rest of the party are fighting the same targets), it is treated as a crime by – for example – the Flaming Fist.
